emb:L630195322.clinical_problem: quality assessment of the standard fetal head ultrasound plane (transthalamic plane) used for biometry
emb:L630195322.patient_population: fetuses undergoing routine obstetric ultrasound of the head
emb:L630195322.model_description: The model takes obstetric ultrasound images of the fetal head as input. A Faster R-CNN object-detection network, trained with a region proposal network sharing convolutional features, locates five key anatomical structures needed to confirm the transthalamic plane. The detected structures are used to automatically score whether the plane meets standard-plane criteria, intended to help sonographers obtain adequate images for biparietal diameter and head circumference measurement.
emb:L630195322.headline_result: average detection accuracy of 80.7% for the five anatomical structures; approximately 0.27 s examination time per image

emb:L2002084150.model_family: Conditionally Rooted Neural Network (CRNN) with wavelet filter
emb:L2002084150.clinical_problem: detection and classification of chromosomal anomalies (trisomy 13, 18, 21) on first-trimester ultrasound
emb:L2002084150.model_description: The model takes first-trimester fetal ultrasound images as input. A Conditionally Rooted Neural Network with wavelet-based denoising extracts features associated with chromosomal anomaly markers and classifies images for trisomy 13, 18, or 21 (Patau, Edwards, Down syndrome). It is reported to be robust to ultrasound speckle noise and is intended as an automated screening/classification tool.

emb:L2001889510.exclusion_reason: study population age not stated as pediatric; abstract notes the disease occurs in both children and adults but does not describe the 40-patient cohort's ages

emb:L2002530412.model_family: machine learning framework (feature extraction, feature selection, and classifiers including SVM) on MRI radiomic biomarkers
emb:L2002530412.clinical_problem: differentiation of pediatric posterior fossa tumor types using imaging biomarkers
emb:L2002530412.patient_population: children with two types of posterior fossa brain tumors
emb:L2002530412.model_description: The framework extracts 300 quantitative imaging biomarkers from MRI scans of two types of pediatric posterior fossa tumors using three feature-extraction methods. Ten feature-selection methods and eleven classifiers were compared, with correlation-based feature selection and a support vector machine performing best, to classify tumor type from the imaging features. It is intended as decision support for distinguishing tumor types non-invasively.
emb:L2002530412.headline_result: best classifier (SVM) accuracy 85.38 ± 3.47%; best feature-selection method (CFS) accuracy 83.85 ± 5.51%

emb:L2002548345.clinical_problem: bone age assessment for growth and development monitoring and endocrine disease diagnosis
emb:L2002548345.model_description: This narrative review compares traditional manual bone-age reading, newer semi-automated methods, and emerging artificial-intelligence methods for assessing skeletal maturity from hand radiographs. It summarizes the shift from manual film reading toward automatic AI-based bone age identification, noting that manual reading is time-consuming, complex, and of variable accuracy.

emb:L2002244375.clinical_problem: radiomics-based diagnosis and prognosis in pediatric diseases
emb:L2002244375.patient_population: children with various diseases studied by MRI radiomics
emb:L2002244375.model_description: This narrative review summarizes MRI-based radiomics research in pediatric diseases. Radiomics extracts large numbers of quantitative, high-throughput features from MRI images to aid diagnosis and prognosis; the review notes that pediatric radiomics research is comparatively sparse and summarizes progress to date.

emb:L2001687195.patient_population: children undergoing hand radiography for bone age assessment
emb:L2001687195.model_description: This editorial discusses the RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Machine Learning Challenge, a public competition in which teams developed automated models to estimate skeletal bone age. No abstract text was provided for this record; content is limited to what the title states.

emb:L625886448.model_family: hybrid CNN (19-layer, transfer learning) + hand-crafted texture features, Fisher vector encoding, SVM classifier
emb:L625886448.clinical_problem: placental maturity grading to assess fetal growth and maternal health
emb:L625886448.patient_population: pregnant women undergoing obstetric ultrasound (placental imaging)
emb:L625886448.model_description: The model takes B-mode and color Doppler energy ultrasound images of the placenta as input. It combines convolutional features from a deep CNN (with transfer learning) with hand-crafted texture features, encodes them with a Fisher vector, and classifies placental maturity grade using a support vector machine. It is intended to automate placental maturity grading, which is otherwise a subjective manual assessment.
emb:L625886448.headline_result: accuracy 94.15% with hybrid descriptors (19-layer network), 3.01% higher than the hand-crafted-feature model and 7.35% higher than the CNN-only feature model

emb:L623911760.model_family: deep convolutional neural network feature extraction combined with clinical/demographic data
emb:L623911760.patient_population: children undergoing left-hand radiography for bone age assessment
emb:L623911760.model_description: The model takes left-hand radiographs as input. A deep convolutional neural network automatically extracts 17 key regional bone-age features from the hand and wrist joint, which are combined with demographic data (sex, population statistics) to estimate bone age. It is intended to improve on traditional manual radiographic bone-age reading.
emb:L623911760.headline_result: mean absolute error of 0.455 years, better than traditional methods and end-to-end deep learning alone

emb:L621001614.model_family: support vector machine using Zernike moment shape features
emb:L621001614.clinical_problem: detection of spina bifida (neural tube defect) on prenatal ultrasound screening
emb:L621001614.patient_population: fetuses undergoing ultrasound screening for neural tube defects
emb:L621001614.model_description: The model takes ultrasound images of the fetal skull as input. It extracts Zernike moment shape features from the skull region and classifies them with a support vector machine to detect shape markers of spina bifida. Oversampling/undersampling techniques address the rarity of positive cases, and the system is intended as computer-aided decision support to help avoid false negatives.
emb:L621001614.headline_result: average F-measure 0.6276 and GMRP 0.6306 on non-sampled test data; accuracy 94% and specificity 98% under the best sampling configuration (400% borderline-SMOTE followed by 50% random undersampling)

emb:L620563519.model_family: k-nearest neighbor (k-NN) classifier on structural connectivity network features
emb:L620563519.clinical_problem: identification of occult spastic diplegic cerebral palsy (brain injury not visible on conventional MRI)
emb:L620563519.patient_population: children with occult spastic diplegic cerebral palsy compared with age- and sex-matched healthy children
emb:L620563519.model_description: The model uses structural brain connectivity networks derived from MRI as input. A k-nearest-neighbor classifier is trained to recognize children with 'occult' spastic diplegic cerebral palsy (no visible lesion on conventional MRI) from large datasets, and permutation testing compares network topology (global efficiency, clustering coefficient, path length) between the occult SDCP and healthy control groups. It is intended to identify subtle structural connectivity abnormalities invisible to conventional MRI reading.
emb:L620563519.headline_result: k-NN provided effective classification results; global efficiency was significantly lower in the occult SDCP group than in controls (p<0.001)
emb:L620563519.study_design: retrospective case-control diagnostic accuracy / network analysis

emb:L617201028.model_family: random forest (feature ranking) and self-organizing maps (SOM)
emb:L617201028.clinical_problem: prediction of fracture healing time in pediatric long-bone fractures
emb:L617201028.patient_population: children aged 0-12 years with lower-limb long-bone fractures at a pediatric orthopedic unit
emb:L617201028.model_description: The model takes features derived from radiographs of pediatric lower-limb long-bone fractures (fracture type, angulation, percentage of bone contact area) together with age, gender, and bone type as input. Random forest ranks which variables most influence fracture healing time, and self-organizing maps then analyze the relationship between the top-ranked variables and healing time. It is intended to help predict expected fracture healing duration in children.
emb:L617201028.headline_result: age and fracture contact-area percentage were identified as the most important variables explaining fracture healing time

emb:L617783153.model_family: regression random forest with importance sampling
emb:L617783153.clinical_problem: anatomical landmark localization on infant brain MRI to support segmentation, registration, and disease prediction
emb:L617783153.model_description: The model takes infant brain MRI images as input. An importance map highlights informative locations in each scan, training voxels are sampled according to this map to address wide morphological variability among infant brains, and a regression random forest aggregates evidence from the sampled locations to localize anatomical landmarks. It is intended to support downstream tasks such as landmark-based segmentation, image registration, and disease prediction in infant brain imaging.
emb:L617783153.headline_result: significant improvement in landmark detection accuracy compared with traditional methods

emb:L617399955.model_family: deep convolutional neural network (8-layer and 16-layer architectures) with transfer learning
emb:L617399955.clinical_problem: recognition of standard fetal facial ultrasound planes (axial, coronal, sagittal) during routine obstetric ultrasound
emb:L617399955.patient_population: fetuses at 20-36 weeks gestational age undergoing routine ultrasound examination
emb:L617399955.model_description: The model takes 2D fetal ultrasound images as input and classifies whether the image is a standard fetal facial plane (axial, coronal, or sagittal) versus a non-standard image. It was trained using CNNs of varying depth (8-layer and 16-layer), comparing training from scratch against transfer learning from an ImageNet-pretrained network. It is intended to automate recognition of standard fetal facial planes during routine obstetric ultrasound.
emb:L617399955.dataset_size: 4,849 training images (375 axial, 257 coronal, 405 sagittal, 3,812 non-standard) and 2,418 test images (491 axial, 127 coronal, 174 sagittal, 1,626 non-standard)
emb:L617399955.headline_result: best recognition accuracy 94.5%, a 3.66% improvement over the authors' previous study; transfer learning improved accuracy by 9.29% and increasing CNN depth from 8 to 16 layers improved accuracy by 3.17%

emb:L619597728.model_family: texture analysis with linear and nonlinear discriminant analysis (LDA/NDA) classifiers
emb:L619597728.body_region: fetal brain (ventricles, thalamus, grey matter, white matter)
emb:L619597728.clinical_problem: automated classification of fetal brain anatomical structures on MRI to improve diagnostic imaging interpretation during pregnancy
emb:L619597728.patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal brain MRI (1.5T and 3T)
emb:L619597728.model_description: The system takes manually selected regions of interest from fetal brain MRI (multiple field strengths, imaging planes, and signal weightings) as input, extracts texture features using the MaZda software customized into a knowledge-based system, and classifies each region into one of four anatomical tissue classes (ventricles, thalamus, grey matter, white matter) using linear and nonlinear discriminant analysis. It is intended as a data-mining tool to assist texture-based classification of fetal brain structures for prenatal imaging screening.
emb:L619597728.headline_result: LDA and NDA combined with dimensionality-reduction techniques achieved 100% sensitivity and 100% specificity (95% CI: 99.79-100) for ROI classification

emb:L621495729.clinical_problem: detection of Down syndrome soft-marker features on first- and second-trimester ultrasound
emb:L621495729.patient_population: fetuses screened by ultrasound in the first and second trimester for Down syndrome markers
emb:L621495729.model_description: This review of computer-aided diagnosis algorithms and techniques, covering 50 papers published from 1982 to 2016, examines secondary-observer systems developed to detect Down syndrome soft markers on first- and second-trimester fetal ultrasound, including nasal bone length, nuchal translucency thickness, and naso-frontal angle. It compares sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy across the reported algorithms.

emb:L605898293.patient_population: fetuses undergoing obstetric ultrasound video examination
emb:L605898293.model_description: The model takes frames from fetal ultrasound video as input and localizes the fetal abdominal standard plane (FASP). It uses a convolutional neural network whose low-level layers are transferred from a network pretrained on a large natural-image database, then fine-tuned on a small set of ultrasound training images to reduce overfitting from limited training data. It is intended to automate standard-plane localization during obstetric ultrasound scanning.
emb:L605898293.headline_result: outperformed the prior state-of-the-art method for FASP localization and a CNN trained only on the limited ultrasound training samples

emb:L601043471.model_description: The model takes measurements of the lengths of 19 hand bones from left-hand radiographs of Asian children and adolescents under 19 years old as input.
